newsitem.title: USA: US spot prods jump on futures, Gulf gasoline buys.
newsitem.headline: US spot prods jump on futures, Gulf gasoline buys.

text.p: U.S. spot oil products prices jumped sharply Monday afternoon tracking NYMEX futures, with Gulf Coast gasoline bolstered by lower recent production and spirited Amoco buying, players said.

Gulf Coast prompt M4-grade conventional unleaded gasoline was offered at about 0.25 cent over December futures, about 0.75 cent firmer than Friday, with any-November material heard traded at 3.15 cents over, players said.

"It started out strong, with front 31st-cycle at a penny over but it came off its highs," said one Gulf player said, who echoed suspicions of other traders and shippers of a problem at Amoco's 433,000 bpd Texas City, Texas, refinery.

Traders said Amoco had bought as much as 300,000 barrels of gasoline Monday morning, and similar volumes late last week. Amoco officials declined comment, but the talk helped lift NYMEX December futures 0.80 cent a gallon, traders said.

Differentials were stable, meanwhile, on New York Harbor reformulated A4-grade gasoline. But diffs weakened about 0.25 cent on NYH M4-grade conventional unleaded as sellers attempted to unload imported barrels, traders said.
Heating oil diffs were little changed, players said, as NYMEX futures rose 0.60 cent.
-- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1632
